---
title: "Figure 10.1: General Government Gross Debt and Financing Cost"
---

![Python: `python/fig-10-1.py`](../images/python/fig-10-1.png)

Government debt in LA7 and other emerging markets for five years, as pairs of
bars. The LA7 financing premium is a black dash across each pair, on a
right-hand scale.

**New in this chart:**

- two series that alternate between rows;
- a two-row label table below the axis;
- horizontal dashes as a series.

## The data

Sheet `data`, 10 rows, without a category column:

| LA7 gross debt | OEM gross debt | LA7 financing premium for LC 10y yields (right scale) |
|---|---|---|
| 50.0 | | 5.13 |
| | 52.3 | 5.13 |
| 32.4 | | 1.30 |
| ... | | |

The rows alternate between LA7 and OEM, for five years. Each row has a value
in only one of the two debt columns. This is how Excel puts the two series
in alternating positions with different colours. The year labels are not in
the extracted data and are typed into the script:

```python
years = ["2003", "2010", "2020", "2025", "2031"]
```

## The script

### The bars

```python
x = np.arange(1, len(data) + 1)
for series, colour in debt_colours.items():
    ax.bar(x, data[series].fillna(0), width=0.62, color=colour)
```

Both series are drawn at all ten positions. Where a series has no value, it
is set to 0 with `fillna(0)`, giving an invisible bar of zero height. So at
odd positions only the LA7 bar shows, and at even positions only the OEM
bar.

### Labels below the axis

```python
ax.set_xlim(0.5, 10.5)
ax.set_xticks(x, ["LA7", "OEM"] * 5)
ax.tick_params(axis="x", length=0, pad=5)
# Separators below the axis: between the bars, and longer between the years.
for xi in np.arange(0.5, 11, 1):
    depth = -0.16 if xi in (0.5, 2.5, 4.5, 6.5, 8.5, 10.5) else -0.07
    ax.plot([xi, xi], [0, depth], color="black", linewidth=0.6,
            transform=ax.get_xaxis_transform(), clip_on=False)
for centre, year in zip(np.arange(1.5, 10, 2), years):
    ax.text(centre, -0.12, year, ha="center", va="center",
            transform=ax.get_xaxis_transform())
```

The first row is ordinary tick labels: "LA7", "OEM" repeated five times. The
second row, the years, is drawn by hand:

- **Separators.** There is a line between every two bars. Between the years
  it is longer (16 percent of the plot height instead of 7), so it also
  separates the year labels. `a if condition else b` picks one of the two
  values.
- **Year labels.** Each year is centred under its pair of bars, at 1.5, 3.5,
  and so on.

With `get_xaxis_transform()`, x is in data units and y in fractions of the
plot height, negative below the axis. See [Tables of labels below the
plot](../techniques.qmd#sec-label-tables).

### The premium as dashes

```python
# Financing premium: one black dash per year, across the pair of bars.
ax_right = add_right_axis(ax, (0, 8), 2)
ax_right.tick_params(axis="y", length=2.8)
premium_by_year = data[premium].iloc[::2].to_numpy()
ax_right.hlines(premium_by_year, x[::2] - 0.05, x[::2] + 1.05,
                color="black", linewidth=1.8)
```

The premium is the same in both rows of a year, so every second row is taken
(`iloc[::2]`). `hlines(y, x_start, x_end)` draws one horizontal dash per
year. It starts just left of the LA7 bar and ends just right of the OEM bar.

The dashes are on the right-hand scale from 0 to 8.

### The legend

```python
ax.legend(
    [Patch(color=c) for c in debt_colours.values()]
    + [Line2D([], [], color="black", linewidth=1.8)],
    [*debt_colours, premium],
    loc="upper left", bbox_to_anchor=(0.02, 1.0), handlelength=1.6,
    labelspacing=0.3, fontsize=8.8,
)
```

Two boxes and a line, built by hand. `+` joins the two lists. See
[Legends](../techniques.qmd#sec-legends).

## The complete script

The full `python/fig-10-1.py`, as it runs:

```` {.python filename="python/fig-10-1.py"}
"""Figure 10.1: General Government Gross Debt and Financing Cost."""
import numpy as np
from matplotlib.lines import Line2D
from matplotlib.patches import Patch

from chart_style import (
    add_right_axis,
    new_chart,
    read_chart_data,
    save_chart,
    set_y_scale,
)

STEM = "fig-10-1"

data = read_chart_data(STEM)

# The rows alternate between LA7 and OEM, for five years. The labels are not
# part of the extracted data; they are taken from the published chart.
years = ["2003", "2010", "2020", "2025", "2031"]
debt_colours = {"LA7 gross debt": "#C7A6D0", "OEM gross debt": "#69B5DE"}
premium = "LA7 financing premium for LC 10y yields (right scale)"

fig, ax = new_chart(
    title="General Government Gross Debt and\nFinancing Cost",
    subtitle="(Percent of GDP; unless noted otherwise)",
    caption=(
        "Sources: Haver Analytics; IMF, World Economic Outlook database; and\n"
        "IMF staff calculations.\n"
        "Note: Financing cost in percentage points is the difference between LA7\n"
        "and OEM's nominal 10-year local currency bond yields. Aggregates are\n"
        "simple averages. LA7 = Latin America 7 (Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Mexico,\n"
        "Paraguay, Peru, Uruguay); OEM = other emerging markets (Bosnia and\n"
        "Herzegovina, Hungary, India, Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, Poland,\n"
        "Romania, Serbia, Thailand)."
    ),
    caption_size=8.3,
    left=0.35,
    right=0.3,
    bottom_gap=0.5,
)

x = np.arange(1, len(data) + 1)
for series, colour in debt_colours.items():
    ax.bar(x, data[series].fillna(0), width=0.62, color=colour)

ax.set_xlim(0.5, 10.5)
ax.set_xticks(x, ["LA7", "OEM"] * 5)
ax.tick_params(axis="x", length=0, pad=5)
# Separators below the axis: between the bars, and longer between the years.
for xi in np.arange(0.5, 11, 1):
    depth = -0.16 if xi in (0.5, 2.5, 4.5, 6.5, 8.5, 10.5) else -0.07
    ax.plot([xi, xi], [0, depth], color="black", linewidth=0.6,
            transform=ax.get_xaxis_transform(), clip_on=False)
for centre, year in zip(np.arange(1.5, 10, 2), years):
    ax.text(centre, -0.12, year, ha="center", va="center",
            transform=ax.get_xaxis_transform())

set_y_scale(ax, 20, 80, 10)
ax.tick_params(axis="y", length=2.8)

# Financing premium: one black dash per year, across the pair of bars.
ax_right = add_right_axis(ax, (0, 8), 2)
ax_right.tick_params(axis="y", length=2.8)
premium_by_year = data[premium].iloc[::2].to_numpy()
ax_right.hlines(premium_by_year, x[::2] - 0.05, x[::2] + 1.05,
                color="black", linewidth=1.8)

ax.legend(
    [Patch(color=c) for c in debt_colours.values()]
    + [Line2D([], [], color="black", linewidth=1.8)],
    [*debt_colours, premium],
    loc="upper left", bbox_to_anchor=(0.02, 1.0), handlelength=1.6,
    labelspacing=0.3, fontsize=8.8,
)

save_chart(fig, STEM)
````
